title: Minimum funnel instrumentation
action: Emit the nine KYC events (start, document, selfie, submission, vendor result, decision, review, account state) with person, session and attempt ids and app/SDK version.
evidence: The extract cannot measure starts, completion, abandonment, retries or time to decision.
outcome: Completion, eventual approval and abandonment become measurable for cohorts starting after release.
participant_names: Engineering · Onboarding platform, Engineering · Mobile, Product · Onboarding, Legal & Privacy
dependencies: Event schema sign-off; privacy review of fields.
effort: M (assumed 3–4 engineer-weeks across backend and mobile)
acceptance: Events for 99% of sessions in a daily reconciliation against vendor transactions; dashboards show first cohort.
rollout: Ship to 10% of sessions, reconcile, then 100%. Logging only, so rollback is turning it off.
guardrails: No images or document numbers in analytics events; access by role.

title: Hold and retry on TECHNICAL_ERROR
action: Treat NOT_EXECUTED / TECHNICAL_ERROR as non-final: retry with backoff (up to three), then hold for manual handling instead of recording a rejection.
evidence: 407 recent rejections with usability TECHNICAL_ERROR; liveness passed in all of them.
eligible: Any decision with a TECHNICAL_ERROR capability
outcome: No final rejections caused by execution errors. Some held cases will still fail once the checks run.
confidence: High that rejections stop; unknown approval
participant_names: Product · Onboarding, Vendor management, Customer Support
dependencies: Confirm how ARQ currently handles TECHNICAL_ERROR (discovery).
acceptance: Zero final rejections with TECHNICAL_ERROR over 4 weeks; 95% of held cases resolved within 24 hours.
guardrails: Retry cap and rate limit so retries don't amplify an outage; cost cap.

title: Daily, then hourly, alerts per reason code
action: Alert on approval rate and on each reason code per country against its normal level; page the owning team.
evidence: Replayed on the extract, the proposed daily rules fire on the first day of 4 of the 4 incident windows, and on 5 day-rule combinations in the prior period.
outcome: Incidents detected within a day now, within an hour once events exist.
participant_names: Engineering · Onboarding platform, Risk & Fraud, Product · Onboarding, Operations · KYC review
dependencies: Daily feed now; hourly needs the Phase 0 events.
acceptance: On replay, alerts fire on the first day of every incident window, with thresholds tuned so prior-period false alerts stay under one a week.
rollout: Start with notifications only, then paging.
guardrails: Review thresholds monthly to limit alert fatigue.

title: Reconcile the control findings
action: Check the 1,223 approvals with birth year 2006 or later, 86 with no screening result and 69 with a screening warning against policy, raw responses, review dispositions and account state.
evidence: Extract findings, not confirmed control failures.
outcome: Each finding confirmed or explained; confirmed gaps fixed. Approvals may fall if gaps are real.
confidence: High that the answer is knowable
participant_names: Data & Analytics, Legal & Privacy, Risk & Fraud, Operations · KYC review
dependencies: Access to screening records and account state.
acceptance: Every record classified (confirmed, explained, data error) with evidence.
guardrails: Escalate any confirmed under-age or unscreened active account the same day.

title: Adjudicate a sample of fraud signals
action: Review a random sample of the Aug 24 Argentina and Sep 14–19 Mexico flags; pull channel, device and cross-transaction data.
evidence: Two clusters of manipulation signals with different volume patterns.
outcome: A confirmed-fraud rate per cluster, which decides the controls.
participant_names: Operations · KYC review, Vendor management, Growth & Marketing
acceptance: At least 50 cases per cluster adjudicated with documented rationale.
guardrails: Reviewers blind to the hypothesis where practical.

title: Diagnose 'no document type' in Mexico
action: Review 100 recent Mexican cases with no document type with the vendor; compare the accepted-document configuration over time.
evidence: No document type for a rising share of Mexican decisions; almost none in Argentina.
eligible: Recent Mexican decisions with no document type
outcome: The mix of causes, which decides the fix.
participant_names: Vendor management, Data & Analytics, Country leads
dependencies: Vendor access to images; data-protection approval for the review.
acceptance: Each sampled case assigned a cause with vendor agreement.
guardrails: Images reviewed in the vendor portal only.

title: Confirm vendor incident scope
action: Ask the vendor for incident reports for Sep 1, 2 and 6, 2023, and the list of affected ARQ transactions; check ARQ's release log for those days.
evidence: A third-party copy of the status page reports liveness incidents on Sep 1 and 6.
acceptance: Written vendor confirmation or denial per date.
conditional: Any SLA credit depends on the contract and on confirmed scope.

title: Report the headline with its breakdown
action: Keep the headline approval rate on all decisions, and show fraud-signal, execution-error and warning shares beside it.
evidence: Fraud bursts and execution errors move the headline for different reasons.
outcome: Faster, correct triage without hiding outcomes.
acceptance: Weekly report adopted by the funnel review.
guardrails: Never report the headline with selected outcomes removed.

phase_label: Phase 1 · Weeks 2–6 · Test the leading fixes
title: Test one guided retake on unclear selfies
action: Offer one retake with lighting and framing tips when liveness returns BAD_QUALITY or FACE_NOT_FULLY_VISIBLE.
evidence: 660 recent selfie/liveness declines; on incident days 174 more.
eligible: Liveness quality failures with no fraud signal
outcome: See scenarios; measured by the experiment.
participant_names: Engineering · Mobile, Vendor management, Risk & Fraud, Compliance
dependencies: Phase 0 events; vendor support for retakes; Risk sign-off.
acceptance: Experiment readout against its primary outcome and guardrails.
guardrails: Fraud-signal rate among retake approvals; spoof labels.
conditional: Only if vendor rules permit retakes for these labels.

phase_label: Phase 1 · Weeks 2–6 · Test the leading fixes
title: Test accepted-document guidance in Mexico
action: Show accepted Mexican documents with pictures before capture and block clearly unsupported choices.
evidence: Rising 'no document type' and unsupported-document outcomes in Mexico.
eligible: People starting KYC with a Mexican document
outcome: See scenarios; measured by the experiment.
confidence: Low until the diagnosis is done
participant_names: Engineering · Mobile, Vendor management, Country leads, Compliance
dependencies: Phase 0 diagnosis and events; confirmed accepted-document list.
conditional: Only if the diagnosis points to document choice rather than configuration or vendor coverage.

phase_label: Phase 1 · Weeks 2–6 · Test the leading fixes
title: Velocity and device checks before the vendor call
action: Rate-limit by device and network and block known-bad devices before a vendor transaction is created.
evidence: Argentina volume roughly doubled on the day of the burst.
outcome: Fewer vendor transactions on attack traffic; no approval gain intended.
participant_names: Engineering · Onboarding platform, Compliance, Legal & Privacy, Vendor management, Growth & Marketing
dependencies: Fraud adjudication results; device data collection approved.
acceptance: False-block rate on a holdout below an agreed threshold.
rollout: Shadow mode first (log, don't block), then block.
guardrails: Monitor blocks of genuine applicants via appeals and support contacts.
conditional: Depends on adjudication confirming coordinated fraud.

title: On-device capture quality checks
action: Use auto-capture with blur and glare checks and a retake prompt; restrict uploads if the current flow allows them.
participant_names: Product · Onboarding, Vendor management, Data & Analytics
conditional: Camera-only capture depends on the existing flow and on the cause being uploads.

title: Pilot manual review of face-match warnings
action: Send face-match WARNINGs, and later a sample of NO_MATCH, to trained reviewers.
evidence: 168 recent face-match warnings and 438 NO_MATCH declines.
participant_names: Compliance, Risk & Fraud, Vendor management, Finance, Legal & Privacy
dependencies: Reviewer capacity, training and quality plan; cost per review.
guardrails: Second-reviewer agreement; later fraud among approvals.
conditional: Requires capacity and quality planning; any threshold change requires risk validation.

title: Invite recoverable applicants back
action: Message people declined for execution errors or capture issues with a retry link and tips for their reason.
evidence: Execution errors and capture issues are the categories most likely to succeed on retry.
outcome: One-off recovery of some past applicants.
participant_names: Customer Support, Product · Onboarding, Legal & Privacy, Data & Analytics
dependencies: Consent and messaging permissions; Phase 0 events to measure.
acceptance: Return and approval rates measured per category.
guardrails: Exclude fraud signals and compliance findings; frequency cap.
conditional: Only for appropriate recoverable categories and with consent.

phase_label: Phase 3 · Next two quarters · Platform work (large)
title: KYC orchestration and decision layer
action: A service between the app and vendors that owns session state, retries, versioned per-country rules, review routing and events.
evidence: Every incident type above needs state, retries and rules that a thin integration lacks (if that is the current setup).
outcome: Faster, safer changes to KYC rules; prerequisite for failover.
participant_names: Product · Onboarding, Data & Analytics, Vendor management, Risk & Fraud, Compliance
acceptance: Parity with the current flow, then rule changes without app releases.
rollout: Shadow traffic, then country by country.
guardrails: Approval-rate and latency parity before cut-over.
conditional: Depends on what the current architecture already provides.

phase_label: Phase 3 · Next two quarters · Platform work (large)
title: Government registry checks (INE, RENAPER)
action: Validate credentials and faces against national registries where the vendor offers it.
evidence: INE flags without volume; face mismatches on older cards.
outcome: Fewer false fraud flags and face mismatches, if prerequisites are met.
participant_names: Compliance, Legal & Privacy, Engineering · Onboarding platform, Finance
dependencies: Commercial terms; registry contracts (e.g. INE requires a direct contract per the vendor).
acceptance: Pilot on a sample with measured agreement.

phase_label: Phase 3 · Next two quarters · Platform work (large)
title: Second verification vendor for failover
action: Add a second vendor behind the orchestration layer for outages and leverage.
participant_names: Engineering · Onboarding platform, Finance, Legal & Privacy, Compliance
dependencies: Orchestration layer; commercial negotiation; parity testing.
acceptance: Failover drill passes with parity on approval rate.
